items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the navigation law, in relation to exempting certain vessels
from the compulsory state pilotage requirement
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4200

SPONSOR: LANZA
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the navigation law, in relation to
exempting certain vessels from the compulsory state pilotage requirement

 
PURPOSE:

To exempt certain vessels from the compulsory state pilotage requirement

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one amends subdivision 1 of section 88 of the navigation law to
exempt certain recreational vessels of less than 200 feet in length from
the compulsory state pilotage requirement pursuant to this subdivision
at the discretion of the board of commissioners of pilots referring to
vessels departing from the Port of New York by the way of Sandy Hook or
by the way of Sands Point or Execution Rocks.

Section two amends subdivision 1 of section 89-a of the navigation law
to exempt certain vessels less than 200 feet in length from the compul-
sory state pilotage requirement pursuant to this subdivision at the
discretion of the board of commissioners of pilots referring to vessels
departing from the Hudson river north of a line running from the foot of
Main street, Yonkers, west to Alpine, New Jersey, or navigating any of
the waters of the Hudson river north of said line and south of the dam
at Troy, New York.

Section three amends subdivision 1 of section 89-b of the navigation law
to exempt certain recreational vessels less than 200 feet in length from
the compulsory state pilotage requirement pursuant to this subdivision
at the discretion of the board of commissioners of pilots referring to
vessels transiting the New York state waters of Long Island Sound or
Block Island Sound east of Execution Rocks or Sands Point, and any such
vessels entering or departing from any port situated on the New York
state waters of Long Island Sound east of Execution Rocks or Sands
Point, or vessels transiting the New York state waters of Long Island
Sound or Block Island Sound east of a line running southeasterly from
the mouth of the Byram River at the New York-Connecticut boundary to Oak
Neck Point on Long Island.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Currently, all foreign vessels and American vessels under register
(arriving from a foreign country) must take a state licensed pilot when
entering or departing regulated waters. The states of Connecticut, New
Jersey and Rhode Island have, or are in the process of, exempting recre-
ational vessels of less than 200 feet in length from compulsory state
pilotage. The Board proposes to amend the referenced sections of the
navigation law to read "Certain recreational vessels may be exempted
from the compulsory state pilotage requirement at the discretion of the
Board." This proposed amendment will make the New York Navigation Law
consistent with neighboring states with respect to pilotage of recre-
ational vessels, and prevent any potential confusion in enforcement
among states.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2018: 8.8935A - Referred to Rules/A.11163 - Referred to Transportation
 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
